answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each agent identity carries a trust score that grows only through verified interactions; new identities start near zero and must wander through a probation window before their actions count toward routing or settlement. Any cluster of fresh identities faces a shared cap on aggregate influence, so mass creation yields diminishing returns. Crossing into higher-trust tiers requires sustained history, a costly bridge no attacker can fake quickly.
